definitions.explanation: A surface of ground that is not flat, especially one that goes up or down.

examples.japanese: この{坂|さか}は{急|きゅう}だ。
{坂|さか}を{上|のぼ}って{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I go up the hill to school.

examples.japanese: {坂|さか}を{下|くだ}ると{駅|えき}がある。
examples.english: If you go down the slope, there's a station.

examples.japanese: この{辺|あた}りには{坂|さか}が{多|おお}いので、{自転車|じてんしゃ}では{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: There are many hills in this area, so it's tough by bicycle.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}この{長|なが}い{坂|さか}を{上|のぼ}って{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}くのは{大変|たいへん}だけど、{健康|けんこう}にいいと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: It's tough to go up this long hill every morning to get to work, but I think it's good for my health.

notes:
{坂|さか} refers to a sloping street or hillside path.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {坂|さか}を{上|のぼ}る: to go up a hill
- {坂|さか}を{下|くだ}る/{下|お}りる: to go down a hill
- {急|きゅう}な{坂|さか}: steep slope
- {坂道|さかみち}: sloping road, hill road

IN PLACE NAMES:
{坂|さか} appears in many famous Japanese place names:
- {赤坂|あかさか}: Akasaka (Tokyo)
- {道玄坂|どうげんざか}: Dogenzaka (Shibuya)
- {乃木坂|のぎざか}: Nogizaka

RELATED WORDS:
- {丘|おか}: hill (landform)
- {斜面|しゃめん}: slope (general term)
- {下|くだ}り{坂|ざか}: downhill slope
